provenance.note: Curated flagship register. Each record carries its own source URLs and the registry ids of the documents it cites; conflicts between sources are listed in _conflicts, not resolved.

note: Five water bodies with sourced history: the three reservoirs in or at the edge of the city that GVMC draws from (Mudasarlova, Meghadrigedda, Gambheeram), the balancing reservoir at the tail of the Yeleru canal (Kanithi), and a natural freshwater lake south-west of the city (Kondakarla Ava). Thatipudi and Raiwada are left out: they are irrigation dams 56 to 60 km away in CGWB's 2025 aquifer plan (Thatipudi 56, Raiwada 60; GVMC's supply sheet of 11 March 2021 puts Raiwada at 76 km) that the dashboard tracks as supply sources, not city lakes. The 11 AMRUT tanks are in restoration-projects-visakhapatnam.json; we have not found a sourced history for any of them beyond its project row. Confidence V = checked against a primary document.

bodies.name: Mudasarlova Reservoir
bodies.era: Built 1902 (GVMC); handed to the town council in May 1903 (1907 gazetteer)
bodies.builder: Public Works Department, for the town council
bodies.feed: Hill streams from Dharapalem and Kambalakonda; catchment 16.4 sq km
bodies.status: The city's oldest piped-water source, owned and maintained by GVMC. On 11 March 2021, GVMC's one-day supply status filed with the National Green Tribunal shows nothing supplied from it, against a normal 0.50 million gallons a day. GVMC's 2018 environmental assessment for an ADB-funded lake project gives its storage as 1.5 million cubic metres, which it calls the original capacity, and 0.75 million cubic metres as the present capacity at full tank level, with no survey or date behind either figure. It says the lake and its catchment have changed over the years, and proposed desilting the lake bed. The same report found two of its three inlets still flowing in: the stream from the Kailasa hills stopped reaching it after a compound wall, a trench and the BRTS road were built across its path.
bodies.cultural_note: The 1907 district gazetteer describes the town's first water works: the perennial Hanumanta Vanka stream near Simhachalam 'dammed up to form a reservoir with a catchment area of six square miles and a capacity of 25 million cubic feet', piped 5.5 miles to a service reservoir near the jail. Waltair stayed on wells. The gazetteer does not use the name Mudasarlova; the stream, the hills and the catchment match it. The park around the lake is one of the oldest public parks in Andhra Pradesh (GVMC, 2018).
_conflicts: Year: GVMC's 2018 IEE (p.7) and DDR (p.8) say built in 1902, as does CGWB's 2025 aquifer plan (Table 9.1); the 1907 Madras District Gazetteer (Francis, p.217) says the works were handed to the council in May 1903.

Capacity: 25 million cubic feet (about 0.71 million cubic metres) when the works were handed over in 1903 (1907 gazetteer, p.217, for the Hanumanta Vanka reservoir it describes); 1.5 million cubic metres as the original capacity and 0.75 million cubic metres at present (GVMC IEE 2018, pp.15, 18). The IEE gives no survey or date for either of its figures.
Water spread: the IEE (p.7) gives 8.1 ha; not shown, because it does not fit the 1.5 million cubic metres of storage the same IEE gives (p.15); present capacity 0.75 million cubic metres is on p.18.

Output: 0.00 MGD present against 0.50 MGD normal on 11 March 2021 (GVMC daily supply status, NGT OA 14/2021 (SZ) annexure); 1.82 MLD in APPCB's 2021 report to the NGT (p.3), the same figure as GVMC's ADB source table (Table 4 of the 24x7 NW sector IEE; demand columns for 2014; draft March 2016, final January 2019); 4.5 MLD in CGWB's 2025 source table (Table 9.1).

bodies.name: Meghadrigedda Reservoir
bodies.feed: The Meghadri Gedda and the Naravagedda; catchment about 368 sq km
bodies.status: A live drinking-water source at Kamarapalem on the city's western side, fed by the Meghadri Gedda and the Naravagedda. On 11 March 2021, GVMC's one-day supply status filed with the National Green Tribunal shows 8.44 million gallons a day supplied from it (5.40 to the Mindhi plant and 3.04 of raw water to the Naval Dockyard (DGNP) and MES), against a normal 7.65. CWC's National Register of Large Dams (2019) lists the dam as operated and maintained by the state Water Resources Department, which reports its level and storage daily on APWRIMS, with a design capacity of 1.169 TMC. In 2018 GVMC prepared an ADB-funded 3 MWp floating solar subproject on the reservoir; its assessment describes the reservoir surface as owned by GVMC.
bodies.cultural_note: Built in 1977 and commissioned in 1979 with 29.31 million cubic metres of storage. In 1989 its drawal was raised to 10 million gallons a day and its storage to 33.1024 million cubic metres at a full reservoir level of 18.60 m (GVMC, 2018).
_conflicts: Year: CWC's National Register of Large Dams 2019 (p.59, 'Mehadrigedda', AP01MH0042) gives completion in 1977, and GVMC's 2018 floating-solar IEE (p.15) says constructed 1977 and commissioned 1979; CGWB's 2025 aquifer plan (Table 9.1) lists 1976.

Capacity: APWRIMS design capacity 1.169 TMC (about 33.1 million cubic metres), agreeing with the IEE's 33.1024 and the National Register's gross storage of 33,102,000 cubic metres; GVMC's 2021 filing to the NGT gives 1.0 TMC.
Catchment: about 368 sq km (IEE 2018, p.15) against 374 (APPCB 2021, p.2, printed as 'Sq.mtr').

Drawal: 10 MGD capacity from 1989 (IEE 2018); 8.44 MGD present (5.40 to the Mindhi plant, 3.04 of raw water to the Naval Dockyard (DGNP) and MES), 7.65 normal on 11 March 2021 (GVMC daily supply status); about 8.00 MGD (GVMC narrative to the NGT, 2021); 41.0 MLD in APPCB's 2021 report (p.2), the same figure as GVMC's ADB source table (Table 4 of the 24x7 NW sector IEE; demand columns for 2014; draft March 2016, final January 2019).

bodies.name: Kondakarla Ava
bodies.feed: A channel from the Sarada river
bodies.status: A natural freshwater lake at Kondakarla in Atchutapuram mandal, Anakapalli district, south-west of the city, fed by a channel from the Sarada. It does not appear among GVMC's listed water sources. It is in the state Water Resources Department's minor-irrigation tank register (MI012625). CPCB samples it as a lake station (2353) under the national water-quality programme: the lowest dissolved-oxygen reading each year was 2.5 to 3.6 mg/L in 2020 to 2023, under the 5 mg/L CPCB prints as its bathing-water criterion, and 4.5 mg/L in 2024.
bodies.cultural_note: In 1907 the district gazetteer called it 'the pretty natural lake six miles south of Anakapalle', which 'swarms with lotuses, fish and wildfowl', one of 'the very few real freshwater lakes in the Presidency'. Its irrigation chapter (p.105) adds that the lake 'has been artificially enlarged'. VMRDA's draft master plan (June 2021) calls it a bird sanctuary with 70 species of birds. It is not on the MoEFCC wetlands portal's Ramsar list or its wetlands of international significance (checked 14 Oct 2026).
_conflicts: Size claim: VMRDA's draft master plan (June 2021, p.52) calls it 'the largest fresh-water lake in the state of Andhra Pradesh'; the MoEFCC wetlands portal lists Kolleru, 90,100 ha, as the state's Ramsar wetland. Recorded, not resolved.
Dissolved-oxygen minimum by year, CPCB NWMP station 2353: 2019 5.0, 2020 3.6, 2021 3.0, 2022 3.4, 2023 2.5, 2024 4.5 mg/L.

bodies.name: Kanithi Balancing Reservoir
bodies.builder: RINL (Visakhapatnam Steel Plant), for the new reservoir begun in July 2016
bodies.feed: The Yeleru Left Main Canal, carrying Yeleru and Godavari water
bodies.status: The tail-end point of the Yeleru canal. The draft Green City Action Plan (IFC for GVMC), posted by GVMC for comment on 19 Oct 2024, says the Yeleru and Godavari source supplies 60 percent of the city's water demand. GVMC's source table for the ADB (draft March 2016, final January 2019; its demand figures are for 2014) lists 9.09 MLD available from filtration at the reservoir. The Visakhapatnam Steel Plant (RINL) began a new Kanithi balancing reservoir in July 2016, on 225 acres, costed at Rs 465.85 crore in its 2018 expansion filing to MoEFCC.
_conflicts: Name: the draft Green City Action Plan spells it Kannati, RINL's 2018 filing Kanthi, OpenStreetMap Kanithi.
We have not found an official date or capacity for the first Kanithi reservoir; the 2016 work is RINL's new reservoir (brief p.2; PFR land and cost tables).

bodies.name: Gambheeram Reservoir
bodies.feed: The Gambheeram gedda; dam at Boyapalem, Anandapuram mandal
bodies.status: An irrigation reservoir on the city's north-eastern side that also supplies the city for part of the year: water goes to GVMC from 1 March to 30 June every year. On 11 March 2021, GVMC's one-day supply status filed with the NGT shows nothing supplied from it, against a normal 0.60 million gallons a day. Most of its 640-acre command area is now built up; about 250 acres were still irrigated in 2021 (APPCB to the National Green Tribunal). CWC's National Register of Large Dams (2019) lists the dam as operated and maintained by the state Water Resources Department, with a gross storage of 3.18 million cubic metres.
_conflicts: Year: 1957 dam completion (CWC NRLD 2019, p.58, AP01LH0008); CGWB's 2025 aquifer plan (Table 9.1) lists 1965 for this source, possibly when the city began drawing from it (not confirmed).

Output: 0.00 MGD present against 0.60 MGD normal on 11 March 2021 (GVMC daily supply status); 8.18 MLD in APPCB's 2021 report, the same figure as GVMC's ADB source table (Table 4 of the 24x7 NW sector IEE; demand columns for 2014; draft March 2016, final January 2019); 2.7 MLD seasonal in CGWB's 2025 source table.
